title.zh: 原子氢质子弹性动量转移截面

summary: Compute the elastic momentum-transfer cross section of a proton on a stationary atomic-hydrogen target using the declared piecewise fit: E < 10 eV uses the low-energy polynomial and E >= 10 eV uses the high-energy polynomial, with the input shape preserved.

capability: H+-on-H elastic momentum-transfer cross section in m^2 from collision energy in eV with a 10 eV branch breakpoint.
operation: Evaluate the H+-on-H elastic momentum-transfer cross section
collision energies -> cross section per energy with the input shape preserved
discovery.model: Empirical H+-on-H momentum-transfer fit with a low-energy polynomial below 10 eV and a high-energy polynomial at or above 10 eV; energy is the projectile energy in the stationary-target frame.
discovery.geometry: None; scalar material function of collision energy with no spatial axis (coordinate: collision energy in eV; output in m^2).
discovery.boundary: Input must be finite and nonnegative; values outside the energy domain take the endpoint value, exactly 10 eV uses the high-energy branch, and the output shape equals the input shape.

identity.relation: the H+-on-H elastic momentum-transfer cross section as a piecewise function of collision energy with a 10 eV breakpoint
identity.direction: collision energies -> cross section per energy, with the input shape preserved
identity.definition: The laboratory proton energy E is clipped to [0.001, 1.01e5] eV. E < 10 uses a seven-coefficient low-energy log polynomial and E >= 10 uses a two-coefficient high-energy polynomial; the cross section is exp(poly(log E))*1e-4 m^2. The two empirical fits are not forced to be continuous; the result has the input shape.
identity.model: empirical H+-on-H momentum-transfer fit; the energy is the projectile energy in the stationary-target frame
identity.geometry: none; a scalar material function of collision energy
identity.coordinates: collision energy in eV; output cross section in m^2
identity.boundary: input must be a finite nonnegative real; values outside the energy domain take the endpoint value, and exactly 10 eV uses the high-energy branch
assumptions: the low- and high-energy fit coefficients retain their declared frozen values; E < 10 eV uses the low-energy branch and E >= 10 eV uses the high-energy branch, including exactly 10 eV.
endpoint clipping does not imply experimental accuracy outside the domain; the low and high segments may have a finite jump, and no unsupported smoothing is applied.
the output preserves the input shape without adding a leading singleton axis; negative energies, booleans, complex numbers and strings are rejected.

inputs.name: energy_ev
inputs.description: laboratory energy of the projectile proton in the stationary-hydrogen-target frame
inputs.constraints: finite and nonnegative; values outside the range take the fit endpoints

outputs.name: cross_section_m2
outputs.description: H+-H elastic momentum-transfer cross section with the input shape.
outputs.constraints: finite and positive; the output shape equals the input shape

preconditions: use the declared laboratory projectile energy and endpoint clipping convention
supported: scalar or array H+-H momentum-transfer cross sections, including exactly 10 eV
excluded: experimental extrapolation outside the domain, a full collision frequency or a Maxwellian average; this function returns only the cross section

failure_semantics.invalid_input: raises ValueError for non-real, non-finite or negative energies
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: evaluation on a valid clipped interval returns a finite positive number

example.description: check the 10 eV breakpoint and the finite positive cross sections on both sides
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.collisions import evaluate_hydrogen_proton_elastic_cross_section
y = evaluate_hydrogen_proton_elastic_cross_section(np.array([np.nextafter(20., 0.), 20., np.nextafter(20., np.inf)]))
assert y.shape == (3,)
assert np.isfinite(y).all() and (y > 0).all()
# breakpoint: CM 10 eV == 20 eV laboratory; 20 eV lab is the high branch.
high = np.exp(np.polynomial.polynomial.polyval(np.log(10.0), np.array([-3.231141e1, -1.386002e-1]))) * 1.0e-4
np.testing.assert_allclose(y[1], high, rtol=1e-15)
example.expected: Three finite positive cross sections with input shape; exactly 20 eV laboratory (10 eV center-of-mass) belongs to the high-energy branch, and the empirical fit may jump across the breakpoint.

scope: the declared 10 eV breakpoint is probed directly: E<10 uses the low branch and E>=10 uses the high branch, including exactly 10 eV; immediate below/above values are covered
input-shape output, input rejection and endpoint-clipping assertions are retained
downstream atomic collision-matrix assembly and independent angular integration use the corrected piecewise definition
verification.evidence_ceiling: the declared piecewise fit and breakpoint behavior are established; no new universal experimental cross-section accuracy is established. Intake acceptance, human scientific approval and licensing are recorded separately
known_limitations: endpoint clipping and the discontinuity between the low- and high-energy segments are inherited; no unsupported smoothing is applied
a previous qualification withdrawal and pending licensing remain recorded; this correction does not rewrite that history

the momentum-transfer cross section of this fit contains the momentum carried by resonant charge exchange (APID 8, 1999, section 1.2, p. 2-3); it is not a distinguishable-particle momentum-transfer cross section, and no distinguishable-particle parameterization exists in this repository

the share of this momentum-transfer column carried by resonant charge exchange is not quantified (UNKNOWN); it is bounded only by the evidence above, and no independent cross-section source covers 0.1-12 eV
